# useHover

> Know whether a pointer is over an element: `[ref, isHovered]` via pointer events.

🟢 beginner · React 16.8+ · Custom Hooks › Browser & DOM · support: client-only

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-hover`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-hover)

## Concept

Returns a callback ref and a boolean. `pointerenter`/`pointerleave` on the attached element flip the boolean; touch "hover" is ignored by default.

## Problem

`mouseover`/`mouseout` bubble and flicker when moving across children; `useRef` + effect versions miss elements that mount later; touch devices emulate hover on tap and leave it stuck.

## When to use

- Behaviour on hover: prefetching a route, starting a video preview, delayed tooltips, analytics.

## When not to use

- Pure styling — CSS `:hover` needs no JavaScript or re-render.
- Essential content or actions: hover is unavailable to keyboard and most touch users. Also expose them on focus or click (as the demo does).

## API

```ts
function useHover<T extends Element = HTMLElement>(options?: {
  ignoreTouch?: boolean;
  onChange?: (isHovered: boolean, event: PointerEvent) => void;
}): readonly [ref: (node: T | null) => void, isHovered: boolean];
```

| Parameter                          | Type                         | Description                                          |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `options.ignoreTouch` _(optional)_ | `boolean`                    | Ignore `pointerType === "touch"`. Default `true`.    |
| `options.onChange` _(optional)_    | `(isHovered, event) => void` | Called on every change; the latest callback is used. |

**Returns:** A tuple: a stable **callback ref** to put on the element, and `isHovered`. A tuple (not an object) because results containing a `ref` property must be destructured anyway (see mistakes).

## Execution flow

1. The callback ref stores the element in state, so swapping elements re-runs the effect.
2. Effect: `pointerenter`/`pointerleave` listeners are attached to that element and removed in cleanup.
3. State stores _which_ element is hovered; `isHovered` is derived, so a swapped element is never reported as hovered.

## Common mistakes

### Hiding information behind hover

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
{
  isHovered && <p>Price: €20</p>;
}
```

Keyboard and touch users can never see it (WCAG 1.4.13 / 2.1.1).

✅ Correct:

```tsx
{
  (isHovered || isFocused || expanded) && <p>Price: €20</p>;
}
```

## Edge cases

- If the element is removed while hovered, no `pointerleave` fires — the derived state still resets because the element changed.
- Pens and mice report `pointerType` `pen`/`mouse`; synthetic events without a pointer type count as non-touch.

## Browser support

`false` on the server and on devices without hover.

## Testing

Tests fire pointer events with different `pointerType`s, swap the element (keyed) to check the reset, and assert listener removal on unmount.
